status_reason: A decision that guides live surgery on patients needs validation beyond a first assessment; the kidney study is an in vitro proof of concept with very high variance and much work remaining, and the surgical use is only an application concept without validation data.
answer: The kidney study cannot be quoted as proof that the sensor is ready for tumour boundary decisions in live surgery. It is an in vitro proof of concept on 14 samples from 7 patients, measured on thawed frozen tissue, with very high variance and unacceptable false negatives. The first step is a laboratory study on paired kidney samples with histology reference, testing NIR against a combined MIR ATR and fluorescence probe.

inline.headline: Test NIR diffuse reflectance on paired kidney tumour and normal samples in the lab before any surgical use
inline.probe: NIR diffuse reflectance fiber probe on the tissue surface
inline.install: laboratory bench on kidney samples; no placement in the surgical field
inline.fiber: Vis-NIR silica fiber (350-2400 nm), which covers the 900-1500 nm LED range of the study
inline.test_against: combined MIR ATR and fluorescence probe on the same samples
inline.not_final_because: Only in vitro kidney data exist from 14 samples; the study used thawed frozen tissue, its variance is very high and false negatives are unacceptable, so in vivo validation is needed before any surgical decision.

problems.text: The kidney study is not proof of surgical readiness: it tested two prototypes on 14 in vitro samples from 7 patients, measured thawed frozen biopsies, and the authors call it a proof of concept with very high variance, unacceptable false negatives and much work remaining.

The study can only be quoted as an in vitro proof of concept that an LED-based NIR sensor captured tumour-related variance in kidney samples. The live surgery scenario is an application concept with no validation data, and the result does not carry over to a different sensor, organ or set-up without new data.
The study used frozen biopsies thawed before measurement; their spectra can differ from real in vivo measurements, so a live-surgery sensor needs fresh tissue or in vivo data.
The study used only four NIR LEDs and reaches about 3 mm into tissue; the LED set must be re-selected for each tissue and cancer type, so the sensor cannot be assumed to fit a new use.

methods.why: It is the only method with kidney-specific data (LED NIR, 900-1500 nm), uses remote fiber probes and penetrates up to about 3 mm, but the present sensor shows very high variance.
ATR fiber probes analyse liquids and soft solids; the ATR depth is 1-6 micrometre, and the fiber must cover the 4000-400 cm-1 range (2.5-25 um), while the PIR fiber covers only 3-17 um.
Tissue fluorescence from FAD (520-530 nm) and porphyrin (613 nm) can add tumour-related information, but fluorescence relies on secondary emission from a few substances.
Raman carries information complementary to MIR but its signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence in organic tissue.

experiment.objective: Test whether NIR on paired kidney tumour and normal samples separates them against histology, and whether a combined MIR ATR and fluorescence probe does better on the same samples.
steps: Obtain paired kidney tumour and normal samples with histology reference, fresh where possible.
Measure each sample with the NIR diffuse reflectance probe over 900-1500 nm, and with the combined MIR ATR and fluorescence probe on the same spots.
Build NIR-only, MIR-only, fluorescence-only and fused PLS-DA models on the same samples.
Validate with segmented cross-validation and randomisation tests, as the study recommends.
Compare the models on the same validation data and check the false-negative rate.
references: S03 kidney study (LED NIR, in vitro)
S04 multispectral ATR-MIR and fluorescence probe study
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: the accuracy target and false-negative limit must be stated by the client before the test.

pathway.key_features: No spectra supplied. Features to check in the lab, from the claims: protein amide I and II near 1640 and 1548 cm-1 (IR), FAD fluorescence at 520-530 nm, and the NIR band at 900-1500 nm.
pathway.path_reason: Surgical use is not an industrial process; the AFS pathway starts with multi-method lab tests before any path A, B or C.

multispectral.why: MIR ATR reads protein and fat bands, fluorescence reads FAD and porphyrin; in a model study the fused data separated tissue classes that neither method separated alone, and the pair was reported for tumour boundaries.
multispectral.test: Build a fused model and single-method models on the same paired samples; the combination counts only if it beats NIR alone on the same validation data. Check first that fresh kidney tissue is suitable for ATR contact, since the model study was limited to liquids and soft solids.

assumptions: The proposed sensor is an LED-based NIR sensor like the one in the kidney study.
The target is tumour versus normal kidney tissue at the surgical boundary.
Paired kidney samples with histology reference can be obtained for lab work.
The live surgery probe geometry and tissue depth are not yet known.
